statement: GEE intervals in a cluster-randomized trial use a t reference on the number of participants minus 2 degrees of freedom (intercept and arm), since each participant contributes one residual to the sandwich variance.
regime: cluster-randomized trial with few clusters (K under 40), GEE
decision: degrees of freedom for GEE intervals

statement: Under the metabolomics, genomics or survey lens alone, a yes/no outcome with no numeric column that reads as a follow-up time is a status at sampling and is correctly analyzed as counted over one period for everyone (a binary model), without asking about follow-up.
regime: Binary outcome; assay or survey lens only (not clinical/dietary); no recognized follow-up column
decision: Whether the follow-up question is asked; binary vs time-to-event analysis

statement: Under prediction, the corrected resampled t of Nadeau & Bengio as Bouckaert & Frank apply it to r repeats of K folds — t = mean(d)/√((1/(rK) + n₂/n₁)·s²_d) on rK − 1 df over the paired fold differences of the primary score — gives an approximately valid 95% interval and test for the difference between two families' cross-validated scores (and a family's and its baseline's) when computed on a repeated k-fold substrate of at least 10 repeats of K folds (default 10 × 5) drawn whatever validation leads; the K(K−1)/2 pairwise intervals are descriptive, uncorrected for multiplicity, because the choice is corrected by BBC-CV.
regime: Prediction; any task; folds not time-ordered; units kept whole; substrate ≥ 10 × K
decision: Pairwise family-difference sentences ('not distinguishable on these rows' / 'X is ahead on these rows') and the baseline verdict's interval
claimed_basis: Nadeau & Bengio, Mach Learn 2003;52:239; Bouckaert & Frank, PAKDD 2004; folds.COMPARISON_REPEATS comment 'Bouckaert & Frank 2004: 10 × 10'; COMPARISONS_NOTE (validation.py:581).

statement: When missingness of the predictors differs by sociodemographic group, the sound missing-data handling for inference is multiple imputation with the group in the imputation model, while complete-case analysis must state its assumption.
decision: Quality-by-group lever routes to the missing-values question with this option Recommended.

statement: For an energy-intake screen under Estimate, if the share of rows removed times the leavers' largest SMD on the adjustment set is below 0.003697, removing the screen (keeping every row) moves the exposure's estimate by less than 0.1 of its 95% interval half-width, so the app recommends 'Doesn't change your numbers here'; from 0.003697 it says 'could bias', and from 0.2 'act on it'.
regime: Dietary lens; Estimate or Describe; energy screen among the exclusions; rows_smd instrument marked calibrated
decision: Recommended disposition of the implausible-reporters noticing in the triage (supplement line vs limitation sentence vs act)
claimed_basis: Calibration: 9 cases (Goldberg plus a ladder of 8 kcal range screens) from 'the dietary proof's simplified pipeline' on the NHANES fixture (complete cases, straight-line nutrients), one band-0 prediction that held (m_pre 0.0012 → m_post 0.011); band_1 lowered from the convention 0.05 to the smallest falsely reassured case; min_cases 5 (convention)

statement: The share of usual intake above the Tolerable Upper Intake Level (UL) is a share at risk of excess only if the recalls include supplements, since the UL applies to total intake.
regime: inference; usual-intake distribution with a UL cut-off
decision: label of the share above a UL

statement: Complementary-pairs stability selection with B = 50 pairs of random halves, each half's first q variables on the lasso path, threshold tau = 0.6 and q = floor(sqrt((2*tau - 1)*p)) keeps the expected number of falsely selected predictors at or below 1 (Meinshausen & Bühlmann's bound q^2/((2*tau - 1)p), which complementary pairs keep under the same exchangeability assumption).
regime: prediction; numeric or yes/no outcome; selection method = stability
claimed_basis: Meinshausen & Bühlmann 2010 Thm 1; Shah & Samworth 2013 (JRSS B 75:55); tau = 'the lower end of Meinshausen & Bühlmann's (0.6, 0.9)' (variable_selection.py:57-59).

statement: A feature whose D-ratio (pooled-QC SD over the study samples' SD) is 50% or less carries too little biological variance relative to technical variance and is removed, with the QC SD frozen before the seal and the study SD taken from each training fold.
regime: untargeted metabolomics with pooled QC samples

statement: Batch entered as a covariate must enter as categories (one indicator per batch), so a numeric-coded batch column must first be confirmed as a code and the column settled as a covariate before the answer is accepted.
regime: batch method 'covariate'; batch column numeric/integer dtype or role not settled
claimed_basis: BLUEPRINT §14.2 (readings confirmed before they change a number).

statement: Under inference, quintiles of a continuous exposure estimate a coarser contrast rather than a false number: they discard the variation within each fifth and assume a step at each cut. They therefore rank below the spline (and the straight line) but are not blocked.
decision: functional form of a continuous exposure or confounder (MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 5)
claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 2 ("a coarser contrast, not a false number"); NUTRITION_PACK §07G; Turner 2010 (contract :2537, "the field's primary-analysis convention")

statement: For an unpenalized regression under prediction, multiplying its coefficients by the calibration slope — the bootstrap's optimism-corrected slope when the bootstrap ran, else the out-of-fold cross-validated slope — and re-estimating the intercept with the shrunk linear predictor as an offset is a sound model update that corrects for overfitting.
regime: Prediction; unpenalized regression family; numeric or binary outcome
decision: The model-updating offer (uniform shrinkage) and the deployed coefficients
claimed_basis: Collins et al., BMJ 2024 (optimism-corrected slope as shrinkage factor); Steyerberg 2019 §13.2; Van Houwelingen & le Cessie 1990.

statement: Under Predict, energy adjustment and substitution are not asked, because the energy model decides what a nutrient's coefficient means (an estimation question) and models that keep total energy predict alike; nutrients enter as recorded beside total calories.
decision: whether the energy question is asked
